text:
The Athletic put it plainly this week: Luke Hughes is shedding his brothers' shadows. At 23 he's playing 24:14 a night for the Devils, with 7 goals and 15 points in 23 games, nine of them in his last ten, including three assists against Washington on November 14.

The goals are the part to hold loosely. Seven on 4.0 expected (the quality of his chances) means 13% shooting, after 4% last season; the chances are real, the rate rarely lasts. Mike Fink of The Hockey News, after Saturday's power-play goal, said the unit's success is about "keeping it simple & not overcomplicating things."

The defensive question isn't closed. Last season Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on the ice than against almost any defenseman (bottom 3%). This year the Devils take 55% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, a good number, though a little lower than when he sits. He still skates like few others: NHL Edge has him in the 97th percentile for 20-mph bursts and 96th for distance. That's the engine; the next step is what he does without the puck.
headline: Luke Hughes is stepping out of his brothers' shadow
